rationale: Lyc. ⲭ = ϫ; ϫⲱⲕ 'fulfill, perfect.' Used of the Father's act of perfecting the Mother of Life before setting her in her place. Distinct from the parallel ⲕⲁ 'set, place' in the same line.
Lyc. infinitive of ⲱⲥⲕ 'tarry, delay, prolong.' Appears twice on this page in the construction ⲣ̄ ⲟⲩⲉⲥⲕⲉ 'spend a tarrying.' Functions as a temporal-extension noun parallel to ⲕⲁⲓⲣⲟⲥ and ⲭⲣⲟⲛⲟⲥ.
Greek φορεῖν 'wear, bear (clothing).' Used of First Man wearing his Five Sons as armor — the Manichaean cosmological motif of the five storehouses/garments donned for combat.
Possibly ⲍⲱⲣⲡ 'be early, first' or ϩⲣⲃ̄ 'fashion.' Verb of action upon a plurality, paralleled by ⲥⲁⲣⲟⲩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'spread them forth.' Sense uncertain.
Possibly Lyc. variant of ⲡⲱϣ/ⲡⲱⲣϣ 'spread, divide' or ⲡⲱϭⲉ 'break asunder.' Action verb upon a plurality. Tentative.
In construction 'number of ⲧⲃⲁⲧ of the measure (ⲡϣⲓ).' Likely a unit-of-measure noun. Tentative.
